subject: Post-call recap: model shortlist, quant trade-study, and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: model shortlist, quant trade-study, and next steps

Thanks for the time today, Aisha — good call. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track: 

Goal summary (as we captured):
- Primary objective: structured extraction from clinical encounter notes (diagnoses, meds, dosages, free-text problems).
- SLA targets: p95 latency < 120ms for single-turn extraction; sustained throughput ~40 req/s per shard; cost sensitivity for large-scale nightly batch runs.
- Compliance: HIPAA constraints; prefer customer-managed keys and audit logs; possible private (VPC/on‑prem) path.

Initial model shortlist (baseline + quantized candidates):
- llama-3-7b-chat (FP16 baseline) — strong instruction-following, low tokenization drift on clinical prompts.
- mistral-7b-instruct (AWQ 4-bit candidate) — promising density vs perf; typically retains instruction quality after AWQ.
- rw-optimized-7b (Redwood-optimized kernels) — runtime-optimized kernels, good p95 on long-context.

Quant/throughput trade-study notes from today's brainstorm:
- AWQ (4-bit) — generally gives ~1.6–2.0x inference throughput uplift vs FP16 with modest quality delta (we expect ~1–3% drop on strict extraction EM depending on prompt set). Good first pass candidate.
- GPTQ (4-bit) — sometimes smaller size but higher variance in tail cases (adversarial prompts can amplify hallucinations); tuning is model-dependent and may require per-layer re-run.
- FP8 (mixed 8-bit float) — can yield ~2–2.5x throughput on supported runtimes/hardware and often better numeric fidelity vs extreme 4-bit quant; not universally available across our Dedicated/Private stacks yet.

Proposed evaluation matrix (what Redwood will run unless you prefer to run locally):
1) Prompt sets: clinical extraction (ACME sample), long-context summarization (visit history), edge-case adversarial set (PII redaction/ambiguous fields).
2) Models: llama-3-7b-chat (FP16 baseline), mistral-7b-instruct (AWQ 4-bit), mistral-7b-instruct (GPTQ 4-bit), rw-optimized-7b (FP8 where supported).
3) Metrics: exact‑match (EM) on labeled fields, ROUGE-L for summaries, hallucination rate (manual spot checks), latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens.
4) Regions: run us-west first; if you need eu numbers we can mirror tests there (extra data transfer/time).

Deliverables & timing (initial):
- Benchmark CSV + dashboard with EM/latency breakdown (attachment: acme_benchmark_matrix_v1.csv).
- Prompt set we used (attachment: acme_prompt_set_v2.txt).
- One-pager tradeoff summary (attachment: quant_tradeoff_onepager.pdf).
Target: first-pass results in 5–7 business days after we have the sample data and confirmation on whether Redwood runs the tests or ACME wants to run them.

Ask from ACME: please share a small representative sample (100–250 de‑identified notes) and confirm security contact for SOC2/PII questions so we can set up an encrypted transfer. Also let us know if you'd prefer the tests run in a Private (on‑prem) environment or Hosted Dedicated; that will affect FP8 availability.

Next coordination: I put a tentative 30‑min technical follow-up on my calendar link (https://cal.com/ben/30min) for next week to review early numbers. If you'd like, we can also include your security lead for the data transfer discussion.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_benchmark_matrix_v1.csv (summary), acme_prompt_set_v2.txt, quant_tradeoff_onepager.pdf
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike O'Neil <m.oneil@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model shortlist, quant trade-study, and next steps

Appreciate the clear recap, Ben — this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications/asks from our side: 

1) PII & redaction: redaction quality is a hard requirement for our pipeline. Can you add a redaction-focused metric (false negatives on PII) into the matrix?
2) On‑prem option: we are leaning toward Private deployment for the initial evaluation because of PHI. Can you confirm whether FP8 runs are available in your Private installer, or if FP8 is currently only on Hosted/Dedicated?
3) EU numbers: eventually we'll want the same matrix run in eu-central for latency/regulatory planning — can Redwood mirror the runs after the initial US pass?

We'll prep a de‑identified sample slice (150 notes) and confirm secure upload details with Mike (cc'd). We may want a short call with your infra person to confirm the Private installer requirements before you run anything.

Thanks — Aisha

--
Aisha Khan
Lead Product Manager, Clinical AI | Acme Health
aisha.k@acmehealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Mike O'Neil <m.oneil@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model shortlist, quant trade-study, and next steps

Thanks Aisha — good points. Quick responses and an updated actionable plan below: 

- Redaction metric: yes — we'll add a PII false-negative rate and a redaction precision/recall column to the benchmark CSV. We'll include automated regex+model checks and 20 manual spot-checks for the initial run.
- FP8 availability: FP8 is available on Redwood Hosted and Dedicated today; for Private (on‑prem) it depends on the installer version and GPU firmware we target. Lauren (cc) will confirm if the current Private package in your region includes FP8 runtime support. If not, we can run FP8 tests in Dedicated and replicate guidance for Private.
- EU mirror: we can run the same matrix in eu-central after the US pass; it will add ~2–3 business days for provisioning and replication.

Updated timeline & owners: 
1) ACME: provide de‑identified sample (150 notes) + security contact for SFTP or secure Transfer Appliance — owner: Aisha/Mike (ETA: by EOW).
2) Redwood: run US pass (AWQ, GPTQ, FP8 where available) across the three prompt sets, add redaction metrics, produce CSV + one-pager (ETA: 7 business days after we have samples). Owners: Lauren (bench harness) + Jonas (quant tuning).
3) Follow-up: 30‑min tech review to walk results and recommend a production pilot configuration (Ben to schedule).

I've attached the initial prompt set and tradeoff one‑pager again. If you're okay with the plan I'll lock in the run and start provisioning.

Thanks — looking forward.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
